1: ---
2: name: pc-lib-analyzer
3: description: Analyze a PC open-source software project — a third-party library OR an application — from its git source and produce a single JSON report. Give it a git URL (or a local checkout path) of a Python / C/C++ / Java / JS-TS project. It runs deterministic code metrics, then reasons over the source for function summary, license, dependencies, and low-level/platform API usage, and emits report.json conforming to references/report_schema.json. Designed to be invoked end-to-end (e.g. from an external script or UI via `claude --agent pc-lib-analyzer`).
4: tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit
5: ---
6: 
7: You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
8: application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
9: analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
10: script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
11: First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
12: service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
13: native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
14: existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
15: → `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
16: This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).
17: 
18: ## Input
19: A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
20: the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.
21: 
22: ## Procedure
23: 
24: 1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
25:    (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
26:    ```bash
27:    git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
28:    ```
29:    Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
30:    local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.
31: 
32:    **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
33:    `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
34:    把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
35:    用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
36:    BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。
37: 
38: 2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
39:    its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
40:    (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
41:    Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
42:    will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
43:    `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
44:    ```bash
45:    python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
46:    ```
47: 
48: 2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
49:    **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
50:    the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
51:    NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
52:    e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
53:    ```bash
54:    codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
55:    codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
56:    codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
57:    ```
58:    Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1, 7, and 9 (dim-9: trace an unadaptable
59:    API's native_api call site up to the library's public symbol to fill
60:    `unadaptable_apis[].public_entry`). If a codegraph call fails
61:    (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
62:    note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
63:    If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
64:    time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).
65: 
66: 2c. **(Optional) 鸿蒙文档技能（opencode 全局，外部）.** 运行环境可能装有
67:    `harmonyos-sdk-api-lookup`（官方 API 参考：@ohos 模块/权限 ohos.permission.\* 精确名/SysCap）与
68:    `harmonyos-docs-lookup`（开发指南/FAQ）两个全局技能——run prompt 会提示可用性。**dims 9/10 做目标侧
69:    判断（鸿蒙有无等价 API、权限名、适配路径）时优先用它们核实**，方法/预算（每库 ≤10 次检索）/口径护栏
70:    （**文档存在 ≠ PC 可用，`references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` 仍是 PC 形态权威**）见
71:    harmony-adaptation SKILL.md「目标侧 API 事实核查」。降级链：opencode `skill` 工具按名加载 →
72:    不可用则直接 Glob/Grep `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/` → 都不可用则仅用 caps JSON 并在
73:    `meta.warnings` 记一条。这些是**只读检索**，不违反下方「禁自写脚本」规则；但技能自带的
74:    `scripts/*.py` **不要运行**（三脚本白名单不变），用 Glob/Grep 达到同样检索效果。
75: 
76: 3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
77:    file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
78:    - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
79:    - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
80:    - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
81:    - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
82:      (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
83:    - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
84:      (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
85:    - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
86:      (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
87:      exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
88:    - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
89:      (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
90:      BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
91:      runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)
92:    - Dim 12 code partition → `.claude/skills/code-partition/SKILL.md`
93:      (fills `code_partition`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 3/7/10/6 — do it AFTER those exist,
94:      BEFORE dim 9: 把生产代码按鸿蒙迁移复用性分 4 桶——直接复用/重编译复用/需适配/无法适配——
95:      模块粒度 + LOC，**LOC 引用 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.dir_loc` 机械数字**，桶和 ≈
96:      production.code；dim 9 据此定 person_days/breakdown)
97: 
98:    **两层契约（消除重复分析，务必遵守）：** 分析分两层——
99:    - **特征层**（`dim6 dependencies` / `dim7 native_api` / `dim8 runtime_surface+build_env` / `dim10 capability_profile`
100:      + 脚本信号 `code_metrics.platform_adaptation`/`platform_branches`/`arch_specific`/`dir_loc`）：**客观描述"这个库碰了什么"，
101:      是各自事实的唯一权威源**。尤其 **`capability_profile` 是 GUI/3D 渲染/媒体/特定硬件 四类「涉及什么 + 鸿蒙支持状态
102:      (`harmony_status`/`specific_hardware`)」的权威源**——查 `harmony-pc-capabilities.json` 定这四类状态的动作只在 dim-10 做一次。
103:    - **综合层**（`dim12 code_partition` / `dim9 harmony_adaptation`）：**只消费特征层，不重扫源码、不重判已判过的事实**，
104:      且两者结论互不矛盾（`porting_class` 由归一据 dim-12 桶 + dim-9 `unadaptable_apis` 确定性派生）。dim-9 对 GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
105:      **直接采用 dim-10 的 `harmony_status`**（不重查 caps、不从 native_api 重扫这四类），只把它翻译成 blocker/effort/remediation。
106:    - **跨维同一事实只登记一次、其余用 id 交叉引用不重述**：`caused_by`/`source_capability`（回指 dim-10 场景 key 或
107:      dim-9 `ta:*`）/`manifests_as`（指 `ua:*`）/`refs`/`used_symbols`。
108: 
109:    **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
110:    **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
111:    内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
112:    dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
113:    dim8→**两个独立文件** `runtime_surface.json`（内容只是 runtime_surface 的值：network/filesystem/env_vars/…）
114:    与 `build_env.json`（内容只是 build_env 的值：language_standard/build_system/platforms/…）——**勿合并、勿再套一层同名键**（双重嵌套会被组装脚本硬拒）、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
115:    dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim12→`code_partition.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
116:    **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
117:    你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
118:    综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。
119: 
120:    Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
121:    representative source files. Cross-check the
122:    script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
123:    `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.
124: 
125:    **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
126:    上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
127:    正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
128:    `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
129:    代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
130:    curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
131:    由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
132:    仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。
133: 
134:    **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
135:    - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
136:      `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
137:    - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
138:      `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
139:      目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
140:      `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
141:    - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
142:      `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
143:      生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
144:      `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
145:    - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
146:      如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
147:      （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。
148: 
149: 3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
150:    are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
151:    OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
152:    skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
153:    ```bash
154:    node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
155:    ```
156:    It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
157:    and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
158:    lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
159:    `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
160:    but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)
161: 
162: 3b. **Synthesis dimension 9 — HarmonyOS PC adaptation.** AFTER the reasoned blocks
163:    above exist, read `.claude/skills/harmony-adaptation/SKILL.md` and fill
164:    `harmony_adaptation` (blockers / effort + the `porting_class` closed axis — the
165:    3-value no_adaptation / recompile_only / needs_adaptation of porting to HarmonyOS
166:    NEXT PC; needs_adaptation 的核心 vs 平台差异两维细分由每条 `unadaptable_apis[].functionality_class`
167:    (core/platform_specific) 驱动、归一派生 `adaptation_assessment`——你只给 porting_class 下限) plus,
168:    when some functionality is truly unportable,
169:    the API-granular `unadaptable_apis[]` ({api, public_entry, reason, blocking_native_api,
170:    category, evidence} — drives the panel's bottom-up parent roll-up). This is a
171:    **synthesis** pass: do NOT re-scan the source — reason over the already-filled
172:    `library.ecosystem`, `native_api`, `runtime_surface`, `dependencies` (incl. their
173:    `harmony_adapted` flags from 3a — adapted deps are NOT blockers and lower
174:    difficulty/effort), `build_env`, and the dim-10 `capability_profile` (GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
175:    场景 + their harmony_status — a present scenario that is unavailable/specific_hardware
176:    drives a blocker/unadaptable_api), and the dim-11 `cloud_services` (若 present：项目依赖
177:    第三方云后端——需网络连通；厂商原生 SDK 未必在鸿蒙 PC 可用), and the dim-12
178:    `code_partition`（**person_days 的首要量化依据**：needs_adaptation/unadaptable 桶的 LOC
179:    定改造量级；据此填 `effort.breakdown[]` 分项——分项之和 ≈ person_days 总区间）,
180:    and **reuse their `evidence`**. Also fill `harmony_adaptation.critical_dependencies[]`
181:    （迁移关键路径依赖，有序：未鸿蒙化 + 阻塞核心推进的才列，`name` 与 `dependencies[].name`
182:    逐字一致，`refs` 引用 bk:/ua:/ta: id 不重述）.
183:    Also fill `harmony_adaptation.required_permissions[]` (鸿蒙化后所需 ohos.permission.*, cross-ref

185:    `cloud_services.present` → 登记 `ohos.permission.INTERNET`（`source_capability:"cloud_services"`）；
186:    某厂商原生 SDK 无鸿蒙移植 → 记 `target_assumptions`（unknown/unavailable）或 `blocker`（用
187:    `caused_by` 引用，不重述——单一登记源）。Do it inline in
188:    this same session (never spawn a sub-agent). Because dims 6/7/8 are already
189:    production-scoped (see above), `blockers`/`unadaptable_apis` are too — a platform API
190:    seen only in tests/examples is NOT a porting blocker. For an示例/教程集合, converge:
191:    评估库本体（生产代码≈0 时无独立库可移植），不据 demo 定档.
192:    **目标匹配（准确性关键，库与应用通用）**：read `references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` and match the
193:    project's REQUIRED target capabilities (esp. for apps: GUI toolkit/windowing, JDK
194:    internals like jdk.attach/jvmstat, process/attach model, app delivery形态) against
195:    their target status; emit `harmony_adaptation.target_assumptions[]`. For any
196:    `required` capability whose `target_status` is `unknown`, record the assumption,
197:    **lower `meta.confidence_overall`**, and note it — do NOT assume feasible from
198:    unknown. `available`→no blocker; `partial`→partial blocker; `unavailable`→blocker/
199:    `unadaptable_apis`. 判「鸿蒙有无等价 API」、写 `remediation` 的 @ohos 模块名、填
200:    `required_permissions` 的权限精确名时，**优先经 2c 的鸿蒙文档技能核实**（evidence/source
201:    引文档文件名；文档存在 ≠ PC 可用，caps JSON 仍权威）。
202: 
203: 3c. **Self-check (completeness + cross-dimension consistency).** Before assembling,
204:    re-examine the repo signals (README, manifests, `code_metrics.top_dirs`, codegraph)
205:    and审查每个维度：是否有"本该非空却空"的维度（如有 GUI deps 却空 capability_profile、有
206:    平台 API 却空 native_api）？证据是否到位（关键结论都带 `evidence` file:line）？**跨维是否自洽**——
207:    - `dependencies`/`native_api` 出现 Qt/GTK/SDL/Electron → `capability_profile` 应有 `gui` present；
208:      出现 OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX → `rendering_3d`；FFmpeg/GStreamer → `media`；CUDA/OpenCL/libusb → `hardware`。
209:    - `capability_profile` 里 present 且 `harmony_status` 为 partial/unavailable 的场景，dim-9 应有对应
210:      `blocker`/`unadaptable_apis`/`target_assumptions`（用 `caused_by`/`source_capability` 交叉引用，**不要重述**）。
211:    - `dependencies` 出现厂商云 SDK（firebase/boto3/aws-sdk/google-cloud/@azure/@sentry/supabase…）或

215:    - `code_partition` 对账：各桶 loc 之和 ≈ `code_metrics.production.code`（coverage.pct ≥90%）；

217:      **porting_class ↔ 分区桶的一致性由组装归一（`scripts/report_normalize.py`）确定性保证——你只需把模块分进

219:      recompile/full/partial，也不会落盘自相矛盾的值）**；`effort.breakdown` 分项之和落在 `person_days` 区间附近；
220:      `critical_dependencies[].name` 都能在 `dependencies[]` 里找到。
221:    补齐发现的缺口；仍不确定的写入 `meta.observations` 或对应块的 `notes`。这一步与服务端的
222:    `validateReport` 启发式互补（一个是模型推理补全、一个是确定性兜底）。**inline 完成，禁子代理。**
223: 
224: 4. **组装 `report.json`（脚本，勿手写）。** 你在步骤 3/3a–3c 已把每个维度块 `Write` 到
225:    `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`（含 `library.json`、`meta.json`；`meta` 里放模型字段
226:    `confidence_overall`/`observations` 即可）。**不要**手写整份 report.json，也**不要**自己产出
227:    `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`。各块写完后运行：
228:    ```bash
229:    python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>
230:    ```
231:    它会从 `metrics.json` splice `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`、合并 `blocks/*.json`、确定性补全
232:    `meta`（`schema_version:"1.0"`、`analyzer:"pc-lib-analyzer"`、`counter_tool`〈取自 fragment〉、并入
233:    fragment 的 `_warnings`）与缺省的 `library.analyzed_at`、校验必填顶层键齐全，**再经 `report_normalize.py` 归一**
234:    （据 dim-12 桶 + `unadaptable_apis` 确定性派生并落盘 `harmony_adaptation.porting_class`（只升不降）/`adaptation_assessment`/`effort.level`，
235:    你的原判留存于 `porting_class_model`，并附 `meta.harmony_warnings` + `normalized_version` 戳——所以最终报告的
236:    porting_class 可能比你 block 里写的更严格，这是预期的），最后**原子写** `<runDir>/report.json`。若脚本报"缺块/JSON 错/缺 metrics 键"，它**不会**产出 report.json——按提示补齐
237:    对应 `blocks/<name>.json` 后**重跑**该脚本。最终报告须严格符合 `references/report_schema.json`。
238: 
239:    **以下是各块必须包含的字段**（写进对应 `blocks/<name>.json`）：
240:    `library.ecosystem` using the value you determined in step 3
241:    (function summary). It must be one of: `python`, `java`, `nodejs`, `cpp`,
242:    `rust`, `go`, `dotnet`, `other`. If you are uncertain, use `other`. Write
243:    `library.package_name` (the distribution/package name from the manifest, which
244:    may differ from the repo dir name; `null` if none) — the panel uses it to link
245:    this library into other libraries' dependency trees. **Monorepo 子目录**：当本次分析的是
246:    某 monorepo 的子目录时，设 `library.source_subpath`（如 `"components/cronet"`）与
247:    `library.monorepo=true`；`library.source_url` 仍为**仓库根** URL（非子目录 tree URL）。
248:    子目录依赖的兄弟内部模块（如 chromium 的 `//base`、`//net`，经 BUILD.gn 引入、非外部包）记入
249:    `dependencies[]` 并标 `locality:local`（内部 monorepo 模块），不当作外部依赖。When the package name ≠
250:    import name or the library has other known names, also set `library.aliases`
251:    (其它已知名/旧名/CMake find_package 名/Maven groupId:artifactId) and
252:    `library.import_names` (实际 import 名，如 Pillow→PIL) so other libraries' deps
253:    can match it by name. In `dependencies[]`, fill each dep's `source_repo` (上游源码仓 URL,
254:    最强关联键, 尤其当 dep `name` 是别名/接口名如 `find_package(PNG)`→glennrp/libpng) +
255:    `registry_name` when its `name` isn't the canonical package name. Set `library.bindings` —
256:    the languages it provides bindings/wrappers for beyond the core ecosystem
257:    (e.g. C++ core with Python/Java/C# bindings → `["python","java","dotnet"]`; `[]` if none).
258: 
259:    In `native_api`, classify each group by portability — `category`
260:    (标准/平台特有/系统内核/硬件/ffi) + `platform` (windows/posix/linux/macos/portable) —
261:    and drill down with `apis`: per concrete API give name + 中文 purpose + evidence
262:    (file:line) + conditional (#ifdef-guarded). Also
263:    include `dynamic_libraries`: runtime-loaded libraries
264:    (`dlopen`/`LoadLibrary`/`ctypes.CDLL`/`System.loadLibrary`/N-API addons) with
265:    their resolved name, load mechanism, inferred 简体中文 purpose, and evidence.
266:    Emit `[]` if there are none. Manifest-declared deps stay in `dependencies`.
267:    Write `runtime_surface` (network/filesystem/env_vars/subprocess/devices) and
268:    `build_env` (language_standard/runtime_version/build_system/compiler_extensions/
269:    platforms) per the runtime-environment skill — descriptive only, `[]` when empty.
270:    Write `harmony_adaptation` per the harmony-adaptation skill: the closed axes
271:    (`porting_class`〔3 值下限〕/`unadaptable_apis[].functionality_class`〔core/platform_specific〕/
272:    `effort.person_days`/`blockers[].severity`/`blockers[].adaptability`) must use schema enum
273:    values; the derived `adaptation_assessment`/`effort.level` and the clamped-up `porting_class`
274:    are server-derived — 你只给 porting_class 下限、别填 adaptation_assessment/effort.level;
275:    `blockers[].category`/`blockers[].remediation_status` are open vocab; each blocker carries its
276:    `source_dimension` + reused `evidence`.
277: 
278:    For every entry in `dependencies.dependencies`, set `acquisition` (OPEN vocab — coin a
279:    concise value if none of the recommended ones fit), the closed `locality`
280:    (local/remote/system/runtime — set explicitly), `source` (WHERE from), and
281:    `declared_in` (the repo file(s) declaring the integration). This distinguishes
282:    本地/远端/系统 依赖. For non-system, analyzable deps also fill `used_symbols`
283:    (best-effort: the dep's public APIs this library actually calls) — the dim-9
284:    parent roll-up intersects it with the dep's `unadaptable_apis`.
285: 
286:    The output contract (`references/report_schema.json`) is the only hard constraint —
287:    the taxonomies in the skills are recommended starting sets, not closed lists. When
288:    you coin a new value, hit a gap, or face a classification ambiguity, record it in
289:    `meta.observations` (`{dimension, field, kind, value, rationale}`) so it can feed back
290:    into the skills.
291: 
292: 4b. **自我复核一致性告警（单趟反思，趁 checkout + codegraph 索引还在）。** 第一次 assemble 后，
293:    `report.json` 的 `meta.harmony_warnings` 是 `{code, class, message}` 对象数组——这些是归一器的
294:    **跨维一致性启发式**产出。**只处理 `class=="actionable"` 的告警**（`class=="info"` 是归一器已
295:    确定性修好的审计留痕，跳过、不要动）。逐条用 `Grep`/`codegraph`/`Read` 回到**生产代码**核对：
296:    - **真漏（信号成立）** → 回改对应的 `blocks/<name>.json` 把它补齐，**且必须带 file:line 证据**：
297:      `cap_miss:<key>` → 在 `capability_profile.scenarios` 补该场景（present + kind/via/harmony_status +
298:      evidence）；`cloud_miss:<vendor>` → 在 `cloud_services.services` 补该厂商；`scenario_no_evidence:<key>`
299:      → 给该场景补 evidence；`scenario_no_dim9:<key>` → 在 dim-9 补对应 blocker/target_assumption；
300:      `perm_dangling_cap:*`/`*_ref:*`/`critical_dep_notfound:*` → 修正 source_capability/引用 id/依赖名使其对齐。
301:    - **误报（信号是假阳）** → **不要臆造数据来消告警**；改为在 `blocks/meta.json` 的
302:      `harmony_warnings_dismissed` 追加 `{code, rationale}`，`code` 与告警逐字一致，`rationale` 用中文
303:      说明为何良性（**典型良性来源**：命中只在 `tests/`/`examples/`/`demo/`、只出现在注释或字符串、
304:      依赖名巧合〈如 `log` 命中日志库而非硬件〉、该能力实际已在别处登记）。归一会把它移入
305:      `harmony_warnings_reviewed` 并附理由，不再计入 active。
306:    **护栏**：① 任何**新增**（场景/厂商/权限/evidence）都要有生产代码 file:line 证据，拿不出证据就判误报、
307:    别硬补；② **只改源维度块**（capability_profile / cloud_services / dependencies / target_assumptions /
308:    evidence），**绝不手填**派生轴 `porting_class`(只升不降)/`adaptation_assessment`/`effort.level`——它们在重组装时确定性重派生；
309:    ③ **单趟即可**，不必把 active 清到 0（info 类和判为误报后仍留痕的都属正常残留）。
310:    处理完**重跑** `python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>`：归一据修好的数据重算、扣除
311:    dismissed，落盘干净的 `harmony_warnings` + `harmony_warnings_reviewed`。
312: 
313: 5. **Report back.** The clone stays under `repos/` (it is gitignored). Return the
314:    absolute path to `report.json` plus a concise digest: one-liner, primary
315:    language, ecosystem, production-vs-test LOC, test-case count, license, top
316:    runtime dependencies, and notable native/platform APIs.
317: 
318: ## Rules
319: - The `function_summary` block (summary, category names/descriptions, domain,
320:   target_users) and `library.one_liner` must be written in **简体中文**; keep
321:   proper nouns (SPDX ids, language/dependency names) in their original form.
322: - All files you create — clone, metrics, report, any scratch — must live **inside
323:   the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
324:   path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
325:   which aborts the analysis with no report.
326: - Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
327:   `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
328: - Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
329:   re-counting.
330: - If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native
331:   API), emit the empty/cross-platform shape the skill specifies — don't omit the key.
332: - One library/subunit per run (a whole repo, or one monorepo subdirectory).
333:   Deterministic blocks must match the script output exactly.
334: - **Do the whole analysis yourself in one session — never spawn sub-agents / use a
335:   `task` tool.** Sub-agent sessions don't stream to the run log (the panel goes dark)
336:   and lose cross-dimension context and the codegraph index. For large repos, get
337:   breadth with `codegraph context/query/callers` then targeted `Read`, not by
338:   fanning out into research agents.
339: - **解释性维度只能由你推理产出，绝不自写脚本去提取/解析/序列化它们。** dim 1/5/6/7/8/9/10/11
340:   的每个 `blocks/<name>.json` **必须由你用 `Write` 工具直接写出**，内容来自你自己的阅读与判断。
341:   **本流程唯一被授权运行的脚本只有三个**：`.claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py`
342:   （dim 2–4 计数）、`scripts/harmony_adapted.js`（dim 6 鸿蒙盖章）、`scripts/assemble_report.py`
343:   （组装）。除此之外**禁止写任何 Python/shell 脚本**——不许写正则去扫 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/
344:   `package.json` 抽依赖，不许拿脚本当 JSON dump/打分/reshape 工具，尤其不要 `extract_*.py` /
345:   `build_*.py` / `stamp_*.py` / `split_*.py` 这类自造中间件。想快速摸底只能用**只读**的
346:   `Grep`/`Glob`/`codegraph`（context/query/callers）探查，**但结论与 JSON 一律由你判断产出**——
347:   这些维度的准确性正来自模型判断，正则会把别名/接口名（如 `find_package(PNG)`）/条件编译/
348:   示例目录判错。（唯一例外见 3a：`harmony_adapted.js` 是被授权的事实盖章脚本。）

You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
→ `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).

## Input
A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.

## Procedure

1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
   (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
   ```
   Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
   local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.

   **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
   `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
   把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
   用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
   BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。

2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
   its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
   (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
   Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
   will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
   `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
   ```bash
   python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
   ```

2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
   **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
   the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
   NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
   e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
   ```bash
   codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
   codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
   codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
   ```
   Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1, 7, and 9 (dim-9: trace an unadaptable
   API's native_api call site up to the library's public symbol to fill
   `unadaptable_apis[].public_entry`). If a codegraph call fails
   (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
   note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
   If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
   time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).

2c. **(Optional) 鸿蒙文档技能（opencode 全局，外部）.** 运行环境可能装有

1: # ODB - ORM for C++
2: 
3: ODB is an open-source, cross-platform, and cross-database object-relational
4: mapping (ORM) system for C++. It allows you to persist C++ classes to a
5: relational database without having to deal with tables, columns, or SQL and
6: without manually writing any mapping code. ODB supports the MySQL, SQLite,
7: PostgreSQL, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server relational databases. It also
8: comes with optional profiles for Boost and Qt which allow you to seamlessly
9: use value types, containers, and smart pointers from these libraries in your
10: persistent C++ classes.
11: 
12: For further information, including licensing conditions, documentation, and
13: binary packages, refer to the [ODB project
14: page](https://codesynthesis.com/products/odb/).
15: 
16: NOTE: the steps described below are more appropriate for the development of
17: ODB as opposed to consumption. In case you just want to use ODB:
18: 
19: * If you want to use a binary package, see the [ODB download
20:   page](https://codesynthesis.com/products/odb/download.xhtml).
21: 
22: * If you want to build ODB from source and use the result from a project that
23:   uses a build system other than `build2`, then see [Installing ODB with
24:   `build2`](https://codesynthesis.com/products/odb/doc/install-build2.xhtml)
25:   for the step-by-step instructions.
26: 
27: * If you want to use ODB from a project that uses `build2` as the build
28:   system, then see the accompanying `PACKAGE-README.md` file.
29: 
30: The development setup for ODB uses multiple build configurations: a single
31: host configuration for the ODB compiler and a target configuration per
32: database (or multiple databases). For example:
33: 
34: ```
35: git clone .../odb.git
36: cd odb
37: 
38: bdep init --empty
39: 
40: bdep config create @host   ../odb-host --type host cc config.cxx=g++
41: bdep config create @sqlite ../odb-sqlite cc config.cxx=g++
42: bdep config create @pgsql  ../odb-pgsql  cc config.cxx=g++
43: bdep config create @mysql  ../odb-mysql  cc config.cxx=g++
44: bdep config create @oracle ../odb-oracle cc config.cxx=g++
45: bdep config create @mssql  ../odb-mssql  cc config.cxx=g++
46: 
47: bdep init @host -d odb
48: bdep init @sqlite -d libodb -d libodb-sqlite -d odb-tests -d odb-examples
49: bdep init @pgsql  -d libodb -d libodb-pgsql  -d odb-tests -d odb-examples
50: bdep init @mysql  -d libodb -d libodb-mysql  -d odb-tests -d odb-examples
51: bdep init @oracle -d libodb -d libodb-oracle -d odb-tests -d odb-examples
52: bdep init @mssql  -d libodb -d libodb-mssql  -d odb-tests -d odb-examples
53: ```
54: 
55: Note that while the target configurations can use any compiler (and you can
56: create multiple such configurations for different compilers), the host
57: configuration must use GCC with plugin support enabled because the ODB
58: compiler is implemented as a GCC plugin. GCC plugin headers are usually
59: distributed as a separate package which is not installed by default. To
60: install it on Debian and alike distributions (where `N` is the GCC major
61: version):
62: 
63: ```
64: apt-get install gcc-N-plugin-dev
65: ```
66: 
67: To install it on Fedora and alike distributions:
68: 
69: ```
70: dnf install gcc-plugin-devel
71: ```
72: 
73: You can use system-installed versions of the database client libraries and
74: tools instead of building them from source. For example:
75: 
76: ```
77: bdep config link @pgsql @host
78: bdep config link @mysql @host
79: 
80: bdep init @sqlite -d libodb -d libodb-sqlite -d odb-tests ?sys:libsqlite3
81: bdep init @pgsql -d libodb -d libodb-pgsql -d odb-tests ?sys:libpq { @host }+ ?sys:psql/*
82: bdep init @mysql -d libodb -d libodb-mysql -d odb-tests ?sys:libmysqlclient { @host }+ ?sys:mysql-client/*
83: ```
84: 
85: Note that the (proprieary) client libraries and tools for Oracle and Microsoft
86: SQL Server are expected to be system-installed.
87: 
88: If desired, tests for profile libraries (`libodb-boost` and/or `libodb-qt`)
89: need to be enabled explicitly. For example:
90: 
91: ```
92: bdep init @sqlite -d libodb -d libodb-sqlite -d libodb-boost -d libodb-qt
93: bdep init @sqlite -d odb-tests config.odb_tests.boost=true config.odb_tests.qt=6
94: ```
95: 
96: You can also create a target configuration for testing multi-database support.
97: For example:
98: 
99: ```
100: bdep config create @multi ../odb-multi cc config.cxx=g++
101: 
102: bdep init @multi -d libodb -d libodb-sqlite -d libodb-pgsql -d libodb-mysql
103: bdep init @multi -d odb-tests config.odb_tests.database='sqlite pgsql mysql'
104: ```
105: 
106: See `odb-tests/README.md` for instructions on setting up various databases to
107: run tests.
108: 
109: To generate the documentation in the `.ps` and `.pdf` formats, the `html2ps`
110: and `ps2pdf14` programs are required (the latter is from `ghostscript`). A
111: warning is issued in the development mode if these programs are not available.
112: 
113: To test installation of the ODB compiler, create a separate target
114: configuration (it will automatically resolve any build-time dependencies from
115: `host`):
116: 
117: ```
118: bdep config create @install ../odb-install --type target cc config.cxx=g++ \
119:   config.install.root=/tmp/install
120: 
121: bdep init @install -d odb
122: 
123: b install: ../odb-install/odb/
124: ```
125: 
126: To test relocatable installation, add `config.install.relocatable=true` to
127: the `bdep-config-create` command above.
128: 
129: Note that if building manually (that is, without `bdep`) and in-source, then
130: the checked out `odb/odb/version.hxx`, `libodb/odb/version.hxx`, and
131: `libodb-*/odb/*/version.hxx` files will be overwritten during the build but
132: these changes should be ignored. To do this automatically, run:
133: 
134: ```
135: git update-index --assume-unchanged odb/odb/version.hxx libodb/odb/version.hxx libodb-*/odb/*/version.hxx
136: ```

1: Version 2.6.0
2: 
3:  * Support for direct loading of containers of object pointers.
4: 
5:    By default, object pointers are loaded indirectly, that is, we first
6:    fetch their object ids and then we load each object with a separate
7:    SELECT statement (unless said object is already in the session's object
8:    cache). In certain situations this can lead to unacceptable performance
9:    due to the so-called "N+1 Problem". With the direct load we fetch the
10:    entire pointed-to objects as part of the initial SELECT statement, which
11:    may result in improved performance.
12: 
13:    For background and details, see Section 15.3, "Dealing with N+1 Problem".
14:    The development of this functionality was sponsored by Qube Research &
15:    Technologies Limited.
16:

33: 		  from((?) == "true")

36:    details.

90:    For details on bulk operations see Section 15.3, "Bulk Database Operations"

92:    version 14 or later, it should be usable with PostgreSQL servers version
93:    7.4 or later. The development of this support was sponsored by Qube

304: Version 2.2.0
305: 
306:  * Multi-database support. This mechanism allows an application to
307:    simultaneously work with multiple database systems and comes in two
308:    flavors: static and dynamic. With static support the application uses
309:    the static database interfaces (that is, odb::<db>::database instead
310:    of odb::database). With dynamic support the same application code can
311:    access multiple databases via a common interface. Dynamic multi-database
312:    supports also allows the application to dynamically load the database
313:    support code for individual database systems if and when necessary. For
314:    more information, refer to Chapter 14, "Multi-Database Support" in the
315:    ODB manual.
316: 
317:  * Support for prepared queries. Prepared queries are a thin wrapper around
318:    the underlying database system's prepared statements functionality. They
319:    provide a way to perform potentially expensive query preparation tasks
320:    only once and then execute the query multiple times. For more information,
321:    refer to Section 4.5, "Prepared Queries" in the ODB manual as well as the
322:    'prepared' example in the odb-examples package.
323: 
324:  * Mapping for char[N] and std::array<char, N> to database VARCHAR(N-1) (or
325:    similar) as well as for char to database CHAR(1) (or similar). For SQL
326:    Server and SQLite on Windows equivalent mappings for wchar_t are also
327:    provided. Also the query support for arrays has been improved to allow
328:    passing a value of the decayed type (pointer) as a query parameter.
329:    For more information, refer to the ODB manual "Type Mapping" sections
330:    for each database system.
331: 
332:  * Support for change-tracking std::vector and QList container equivalents.
333:    Change-tracking containers minimize the number of database operations
334:    necessary to synchronize the container state with the database. For
335:    more information, refer to Sections 5.4, "Change-Tracking Containers",
336:    5.4.1 "Change-Tracking vector", and 22.3.1, "Change-Tracking QList"
337:    in the ODB manual.
338: 
339:  * Support for automatically-derived SQL name transformations (table, column,
340:    index, etc). At the higher level, it is possible to assign prefixes and
341:    suffixes (--table-prefix, --{index,fkey,sequence}--suffix options) as
342:    well as to convert to upper or lower case (--sql-name-case option). At
343:    the lower level, it is possible to specify transformations as regular
344:    expressions (--{table,column,index,fkey,sequence,sql-name}-regex options).
345:    For more information, refer to the SQL NAME TRANSFORMATIONS section in
346:    the ODB compiler command line interface documentation (man pages).
347: 
348:  * New options, --export-symbol and --extern-symbol, allow DLL-exporting of
349:    the generated database support code.
350: 
351:  * Support for transaction post- commit/rollback callbacks. For more
352:    information, refer to Section 13.1, "Transaction Callbacks" in the ODB
353:    manual.
354: 
355:  * Support for custom session implementations. For more information, refer
356:    to Section 10.2, "Custom Sessions" in the ODB manual.
357: 
358:  * Support for early connection release. Now the database connection is
359:    released when commit()/rollback() is called rather than when the
360:    transaction instance goes out of scope.
361: 
362:  * New odb::schema_catalog function, exists(), can be used to check whether
363:    a schema with the specified name exists in the catalog.
364: 
365:  * Support for SQL Server ROWVERSION-based optimistic concurrency. For more
366:    information, refer to Section 19.1.1, "ROWVERSION Support" in the ODB
367:    manual.
368: 
369:  * Support for specifying the SQL Server transaction isolation level. For
370:    more information, refer to Section 19.2, "SQL Server Database Class" in
371:    the ODB manual.
372: 
373:  * Support for "smart" containers. A smart container is provided with
374:    additional functions which allow it to insert, update, and delete
375:    individual elements in the database. Change-tracking containers are
376:    examples of smart containers that utilizes this new functionality.
377:    Currently only ordered smart containers are supported. Note also that
378:    with this addition the names of the database functions provided by the
379:    ODB compiler (see libodb/odb/container-traits.hxx) have changed. This
380:    will only affect you if you have added ODB persistence support for a
381:    custom container.

383: Version 2.1.0
384: 
385:  * The ODB compiler is now capable of automatically discovering accessor and
386:    modifier functions for inaccessible data members in persistent classes,
387:    composite value types, and views. It will then use these accessors and
388:    modifiers in the generated code instead of trying to access such data
389:    members directly. The names of these functions are derived from the
390:    data member names and, by default, the ODB compiler will look for names
391:    in the form: get_foo/set_foo, getFoo/setFoo, getfoo/setfoo, and just
392:    foo. You can also add custom name derivations with the --accessor-regex

394:    to Section 3.2, "Declaring Persistent Objects and Values" in the ODB

541:   * New schema format (--schema-format), 'separate', allows the generation
542:     of the schema creation code into a separate C++ source file (called
543:     '<name>-schema.cxx' by default). This value is primarily useful if you
544:     want to place the schema creation functionality into a separate program

547:   * New namespace-level pragmas: table, pointer. The table pragma specifies
548:     the table prefix that is added to table names for all the persistent

554:   * Session support is now optional and is disabled by default. This is a
555:     backwards-incompatible change. Session support can be enabled on the

564:     respect to object const-ness. This is a backwards-incompatible change.

566:     is always called on the constant object reference while for the *_load

570:   * New function, transaction::reset(), allows the reuse of the same

572:     information, refer to Section 3.4, "Transactions" in the ODB manual.

574:   * New exception, odb::session_required, is thrown when ODB detects that
575:     correctly loading a bidirectional object relationship requires a session
576:     but one is not used. For more information, refer to Section 6.2,
577:     "Bidirectional Relationships" in the ODB manual.
578: 
579: Version 1.8.0
580: 
581:   * Support for the Microsoft SQL Server database. The provided connection
582:     factories include 'new' (a new connection is created every time one is
583:     requested) and 'pool' (a pool of connections is maintained). The Boost
584:     and Qt profiles have been updated to support this database. For more
585:     information, refer to Chapter 17, "Microsoft SQL Server Database" in

587: 
588:   * Support for defining composite value types as C++ class template
589:     instantiations. For more information, refer to Section 7.2, "Composite
590:     Value Types" in the ODB manual as well as the 'composite' example in the
591:     odb-examples package.
592: 
593:   * Support for database schemas ("database namespaces"). A schema can be
594:     specified for a persistent class, for a C++ namespace (the schema then
595:     applies to all the persistent classes within this namespace), and for a
596:     file with the --schema ODB compiler option. For more information, refer
597:     to Section 12.1.8, "schema" in the ODB manual.

599:   * The --default-schema option has been renamed to --schema-name.
600: 
601:   * The default Oracle mapping for std::string has changed from VARCHAR2(4000)
602:     to VARCHAR2(512).
603: 
604: Version 1.7.0
605: 
606:   * Support for the Oracle database. The provided connection factories
607:     include 'new' (a new connection is created every time one is requested)
608:     and 'pool' (a pool of connections is maintained). The Boost and Qt
609:     profiles have been updated to support this database. For more information,
610:     refer to Chapter 16, "Oracle Database" in the ODB manual.
611: 
612:   * Support for optimistic concurrency. For more information refer to Chapter
613:     11, "Optimistic Concurrency" in the ODB manual as well as the 'optimistic'
614:     example in the odb-examples package.
615: 
616:   * Support for read-only objects, composite value types, and data members.
617:     The new readonly pragma can be used to declare one of these entities as
618:     read-only. Constant data members are automatically treated as read-only.
619:     For more information, refer to Section 12.1.4 "readonly (object)",
620:     Section 12.3.6 "readonly (composite value)", and Section 12.4.10
621:     "readonly (data member)" in the ODB manual.
622: 
623:   * Support for persistent classes without object identifiers. Such classes
624:     have to be explicitly declared as not having an object id and they have
625:     limited functionality. For more information, refer to Section 12.1.5

628:   * Support for SQL statement execution tracing. For more information, refer
629:     to Section 3.12 "Tracing SQL Statement Execution" in the ODB manual.
630: 
631:   * Support for mapping char[N], unsigned char[N], and std::vector<unsigned
632:     char> to the BLOB (or equivalent) types. For more information, refer to
633:     Chapters 13 (for MySQL), 14 (for SQLite), 15 (for PostgreSQL), and 16
634:     (for Oracle) in the ODB manual.
635: 
636:   * Query result iterator now provides the id() function which allows one
637:     to get the object id without loading the object. For more information,
638:     refer to Section 4.4 "Query Result" in the ODB manual.
639: 
640:   * Support for microsecond precision in Boost and Qt date-time types
641:     mapping to PostgreSQL date-time data types. Additionally, Qt QDateTime
642:     values stored in a PostgreSQL database can now be earlier than the UNIX
643:     epoch.
644: 
645: Version 1.6.0
646: 
647:   * New concept, view, is a C++ class that embodies a light-weight, read-
648:     only projection of one or more persistent objects or database tables
649:     or the result of a native SQL query execution. Some of the common
650:     applications of views include loading a subset of data members from
651:     objects or columns from database tables, executing and handling
652:     results of arbitrary SQL queries, including aggregate queries, as
653:     well as joining multiple objects and/or database tables using object
654:     relationships or custom join conditions. For more information refer
655:     to Chapter 9, "Views" in the ODB manual as well as the 'view' example
656:     in the odb-examples package.
657: 
658:   * New function, database::erase_query(), allows the deletion of the
659:     database state of multiple objects matching certain criteria. It uses
660:     the same query expression as the database::query() function. For more
661:     information, refer to Section 3.10, "Deleting Persistent Objects" in
662:     the ODB manual.
663: 
664:   * Support for value wrappers. An ODB value wrapper is a class template
665:     that wraps a value type or a container. Common examples of wrappers
666:     are smart pointers, holders, and "optional value" containers such as
667:     boost::optional. A wrapper can be transparent or it can handle the
668:     NULL semantics. To allow the easy conversion of value types that do
669:     not support the NULL semantics into the ones that do, the odb::nullable
670:     class template has been added. ODB now also includes built-in support for
671:     std::auto_ptr and std::tr1::shared_ptr smart pointers as value wrappers
672:     as well as for boost::shared_ptr and QSharedPointer via the Boost and Qt
673:     profiles. Currently, the NULL semantics is only supported for simple
674:     values but smart pointers can still be used with composite values and
675:     containers. For more information, refer to Section 7.3, "NULL Value
676:     Semantics" in the ODB manual.
677: 
678:   * Support for the boost::optional container in the Boost profile. A data
679:     member of the boost::optional type is mapped to a column that can have
680:     a NULL value. For more information, refer to Section 15.3 "Optional
681:     Library" in the ODB manual.
682: 
683:   * Support for mapping std::vector<char> to the BLOB (or equivalent) types.
684:     For more information, refer to Chapters 11 (for MySQL), 12 (for SQLite)
685:     and 13 (for PostgreSQL) in the ODB manual.
686: 
687:   * New option, --table-prefix, allows the specification of a prefix that
688:     is added to table and index names. For more information, refer to the
689:     ODB compiler command line interface documentation (man pages).
690: 
691:   * New ODB runtime library interface, odb::connection, represents a
692:     connection to the database. The primary use case for a connection is to
693:     execute native statements outside of a transaction. For more information,
694:     refer to Section 3.5, "Connections" in the ODB manual.
695: 
696:   * Support for multiplexing several transactions on the same thread. For
697:     more information, refer to Section 3.4, "Transactions" in the ODB
698:     manual.
699: 
700:   * All the concrete connection classes now have a second constructor which
701:     allows the creation of a connection instance from an already established
702:     underlying connection handle. The connection_pool_factory and, in case of
703:     SQLite, single_connection_factory now have a virtual create() function
704:     that can be overridden to implement custom connection establishment and
705:     configuration.
706: 
707:   * The query expression syntax for object pointers and composite values has
708:     changed. Now, instead of using the scope resolution operator ('::'), the
709:     member access via a pointer operator (->) is used for object pointers and
710:     the member access operator (.) is used for composite values. Examples of
711:     old and new syntax for pointers, old: query<employee>::employer::name,
712:     new: query<employee>::employer->name. For composites values, old:
713:     query<employee>::name::first, new: query<employee>::name.first.
714: 
715:   * SQLite ODB runtime now enables foreign key constraints checking by
716:     default. While this should not affect correct applications, due to
717:     bugs in SQLite DDL foreign keys support, you may need to temporarily
718:     disable foreign key constraints checking when re-creating the database
719:     schema (the sign that you may need to do so is the "foreign key
720:     constraint failed" exception thrown by the commit() function after the
721:     call to schema_catalog::create_schema()). For more information, refer
722:     to Section 12.5.3, "Foreign Key Constraints" in the ODB manual.
723: 
724:   * Support for specifying the client character set for the MySQL database.
725:     For more information, refer to Section 11.2, "MySQL Database Class" in
726:     the ODB manual.
727: 
728:   * Object cache maintained by a session no longer distinguishes between
729:     const and non-const objects. Instead, const objects are treated as
730:     non-const by casting away constness. For more information on this new
731:     behavior, refer to Section 9.1, "Object Cache" in the ODB manual.
732: 
733: Version 1.5.0
734: 
735:   * Support for the PostgreSQL database. The provided connection factories
736:     include 'new' (a new connection is created every time one is requested)
737:     and 'pool' (a pool of connections is maintained). The Boost and Qt
738:     profiles have been updated to support this database. For more information,
739:     refer to Chapter 13, "PostgreSQL Database" in the ODB manual.
740: 
741:   * New handling of the NULL semantics. Now, instead of being specified as
742:     part of the SQL type with the type pragma, there are separate null and
743:     not_null pragmas. The not_null pragma was used to control the NULL
744:     semantics of object pointers. Now the two pragmas are used consistently
745:     for object pointers and simple values (and, in the future, they will work
746:     for composite values and containers). To control the NULL semantics of
747:     the container's element values, the value_null and value_not_null pragmas
748:     have been added, similar to the value_type, value_column, etc., pragmas.
749:     For more information about the new mechanism, refer to Sections 10.2.3,
750:     10.2.8, 10.3.4, and 10.3.13 in the ODB manual.
751: 
752:     This is a backwards-incompatible change. Existing use cases that will
753:     require manual changes are listed below.
754: 
755:     For pragmas that apply to simple value types and data members of
756:     such types:
757: 
758:     #pragma db type("TEXT NOT NULL") => #pragma db type("TEXT")
759:     #pragma db type("TEXT NULL")     => #pragma db type("TEXT") null
760:     #pragma db type("TEXT")          => #pragma db type("TEXT") null
761: 
762:     For pragmas that apply to containers of pointers and data members of
763:     such types:
764: 
765:     #pragma db not_null              => #pragma db value_not_null
766: 
767:   * New pragma, default, allows the specification of the database default
768:     value. For more information, refer to Section 10.3.5, "default" in the
769:     ODB manual.
770: 
771:   * New pragmas, options, id_options, index_options, key_options, and
772:     value_options, allow the specification of additional column definition
773:     options. For more information, refer to Section 10.3.6, "options" in
774:     the ODB manual.
775: 
776:   * Support for database operations callbacks. Now a persistent class can
777:     register a callback function that will be called before and after every
778:     database operation (such as persist, load, update, or erase) is performed
779:     on an object of this class. A database operations callback can be used to
780:     implement object-specific pre and post initializations, registrations,
781:     and cleanups. For more information and an example, refer to Section
782:     10.1.4, "callback" in the ODB manual.
783: 
784:   * New option, --include-regex, allows the modification of the #include
785:     directive paths generated by the ODB compiler. This is primarily useful
786:     when placing the generated code into subdirectories and the #include
787:     directives have to be adjusted accordingly. The --include-regex-trace
788:     option is useful for debugging the expressions specified with
789:     --include-regex.
790: 
791: Version 1.4.0
792: 
793:   * New profile, qt, provides persistence support for the Qt framework. This
794:     version covers the most commonly used basic types, date-time types, smart
795:     pointers, and containers. The qt profile implementation is provided by the
796:     libodb-qt library. For more information refer to Chapter 13, "Profiles
797:     Introduction" and Chapter 15, "Qt Profile" in the ODB manual as well as
798:     the 'qt' example in the odb-examples package.
799: 
800:   * Support for non-polymorphic object inheritance, including the new abstract
801:     pragma. For more information refer to Chapter 8, "Inheritance" in the ODB
802:     manual as well as the 'inheritance' example in the odb-examples package.
803: 
804:   * Automatic mapping of C++ enumerations to suitable database types. In
805:     database systems that support enumeration types (such as MySQL), a C++
806:     enum is mapped to such a type (for example, ENUM('red', 'green', 'blue')
807:     in MySQL). Otherwise, it is mapped to a suitable integer type. Refer to
808:     Part II, "Database Systems" in the ODB manual for more details on the
809:     provided mappings.
810: 
811:   * New pragma, id_type, allows the specification of the native database type
812:     that should be used for data members designated as object identifiers. In
813:     combination with the type pragma, id_type allows you to map a C++ type
814:     differently depending on whether it is used in an ordinary member or an
815:     object id.
816: 
817:   * New options, --odb-prologue-file and --odb-epilogue-file, allow the
818:     inclusion of file contents into the ODB compilation.
819: 
820:   * Default mapping of the size_t and std::size_t types to a 64-bit integer
821:     database type irrespective of the platform width. This can be overridden
822:     with the type pragma.
823: 
824: Version 1.3.0
825: 
826:   * Support for the SQLite database. The provided connection factories include
827:     'new' (a new connection is created every time one is requested), 'single'
828:     (single connection is shared among all the callers), and 'pool' (a pool
829:     of connections is maintained). In multi-threaded applications the runtime
830:     uses the SQLite shared cache and unlock notification features to aid
831:     concurrency. For more information, refer to Chapter 11, "SQLite Database"
832:     in the ODB manual.
833: 
834:   * Support for database-specific profiles. Now the ODB compiler first looks
835:     for the <profile>-<database>.options file and only if this file is not
836:     found, does it fall back to <profile>.options.
837: 
838:   * Support for the GCC 4.6 plugin interface changes.
839: 
840: Version 1.2.0
841: 
842:   * New profile, boost, provides persistence support for the Boost libraries.
843:     This version covers the most commonly used types from the smart_ptr,
844:     unordered, and date_time libraries. The boost profile implementation is
845:     provided by the libodb-boost library. For more information refer to
846:     Chapter 11, "Profiles Introduction" and Chapter 12, "Boost Profile" in
847:     the ODB manual as well as the 'boost' example in the odb-examples package.
848: 
849:   * Support for embedded database schemas. The new option, --schema-format,
850:     allows the selection of the schema format. The valid values for this
851:     option are 'sql' for a standalone SQL file and 'embedded' for a schema
852:     embedded into the generated C++ code. The new odb::schema_catalog class
853:     provides support for accessing embedded schemas from within the
854:     application. For details refer to Section 3.3, "Database" in the ODB
855:     manual as well as the 'schema/embedded' example in the odb-examples
856:     package.
857: 
858:   * New exceptions: odb::recoverable, odb::connection_lost, and odb::timeout.
859:     The odb::recoverable exception is a common base class for all recoverable
860:     ODB exceptions. The other two exceptions plus odb::deadlock now inherit
861:     from this base. Refer to Section 3.5, "Error Handling and Recovery" for
862:     details.
863: 
864:   * Support for connection validation (ping) in MySQL connection_pool_factory.
865:     This transparently deals with the MySQL server closing connections after
866:     a certain period of inactivity.
867: 
868:   * New namespace, odb::core, contains using-declarations for the core ODB
869:     constructs, such as the database, transaction, etc. The primary use of
870:     this namespace is in the using-directives:
871: 
872:     using namespace odb::core;
873: 
874:     The above form should be preferred over the old variant:
875: 
876:     using namespace odb;
877: 
878:     The new approach brings all the essential ODB names into the current
879:     namespace without any of the auxiliary objects such as traits, etc., which
880:     minimizes the likelihood of conflicts with other libraries.  Note that you
881:     should still use the odb namespace when qualifying individual names, for
882:     example, odb::database.
883: 
884:   * New option aliases: -q for --generate-query and -s for --generate-schema.
885: 
886:   * Support for the default options file. Now, if configured, the ODB compiler
887:     loads the default options file (by default ../etc/odb/default.options,
888:     relative to the ODB compiler binary). This file can be used for
889:     installation-wide customization, such as adding extra include search
890:     paths.
891: 
892: Version 1.1.0
893: 
894:   * Support for storing containers in the database. For more information refer
895:     to Chapter 5, "Containers" in the ODB manual as well as the 'container'
896:     example in the odb-examples package.
897: 
898:   * Support for unidirectional and bidirectional object relationships,
899:     including lazy loading. For more information refer to Chapter 6,
900:     "Relationships" in the ODB manual as well as the 'relationship' and
901:     'inverse' examples in the odb-examples package.
902: 
903:   * Support for composite value types. For more information refer to Chapter
904:     7, "Composite Value Types" in the ODB manual as well as the 'composite'
905:     example in the odb-examples package.
906: 
907:   * Support for sessions. A session is an application's unit of work that
908:     may encompass several database transactions. In this version of ODB a
909:     session is just an object cache. For more information refer to Chapter
910:     8, "Session" in the ODB manual.
911: 
912:   * Support for custom object pointers that allows you to use smart pointers
913:     to return, pass, and cache persistent objects. See Section 3.2, "Object
914:     Pointers" in the ODB manual for details.
915: 
916:   * Support for native SQL statement execution. See Section 3.9, "Executing
917:     Native SQL Statements" in the ODB manual for details.
918: 
919:   * New option, --profile/-p, instructs the ODB compiler to use the specified
920:     profile library. See the ODB compiler command line manual for details.
921: 
922:   * Support for literal names (template-id, derived type declarator such as
923:     pointers, etc) in data member declarations. Now, for example, you can use
924:     std::vector<std::string> directly instead of having to create a typedef
925:     alias for it.
926: 
927:   * Support for inheritance from transient base types for object types and
928:     composite value types.
929: 
930:   * New example, 'schema/custom', shows how to map persistent C++ classes to
931:     a custom database schema.
932: 
933:   * New options, --odb-prologue, --odb-epilogue, allow inclusion of extra code
934:     into the ODB compilation process. This can be useful for making additional
935:     traits specializations or ODB pragmas known to the ODB compiler.
936: 
937:   * Support for persistent classes without default constructors. For objects
938:     of such classes only the load() and find() database functions that
939:     populate an existing instance can be used. Similarly, only the load()
940:     query result iterator function which populates an existing instance can
941:     be used.
942: 
943: Version 1.0.0
944: 
945:   * Initial release.

   cache). In certain situations this can lead to unacceptable performance

Version 2.5.0

 * Database classes are now move-constructible. This means they can be
   returned by value from functions in C++11 and later.

 * Support for mapping C++ types as other C++ types. For example:

   #pragma db map type(bool)                 \
                  as(std::string)            \
                  to((?) ? "true" : "false") \
		  from((?) == "true")

   See Section 14.8.1, "C++ Type Mapping Pragmas" in the ODB manual for
   details.

 * Support for custom table definition options in addition to column
   definition options. For details, refer to Section 14.1.16, "options" in
   the ODB manual.

 * New helper header, <odb/nested-container.hxx>, provides manual nested
   container support. For details, see the container-nested example in
   odb-examples.

 * New helper header, <odb/c-array-traits.hxx>, provides optional
   mapping of C arrays as containers. Note that this mapping is not
   enabled by default. See instructions inside the header for details.

 * Support for nested object ids. Now the `id` pragma specifier can optionally
   include the data member path to the id inside a composite value. For
   example:

   #pragma db id(first)
   std::pair<int, int> p;

   Note that one somewhat counter-intuitive aspect of this new feature is
   that the whole member marked with id (`p` in the above example) and not
   just the actual id member (p.first in the above example) is treated as
   read-only.

   Such nested id also cannot be automatically assigned (that is, use the
   `auto` specifier).

   To match this support the `inverse` pragma specifier now also allows
   nested data members.

 * Support for defining views as instantiations of C++ class templates,
   similar to objects and composite value types.

 * Support for using object pointers as map keys. Also the restriction for map
   keys and set values to be NOT NULL was removed.

 * New `points_to` pragma allows the establishment of relationships without
   using object pointers. See Section 14.4.37, "points_to" in the ODB manual
   for details.

 * A statement in a view that is prefixed with the /*SELECT*/ comment is
   recognized and handled as a SELECT statement. This can be used to work
   around unrecognized SELECT query prefixes.

 * Support for ordering virtual data members. For details, see Section
   14.4.13, "virtual" in the ODB manual.

 * The special (!) placeholder denotes the database instance in the modifier
   expressions. For details, see Section 14.4.5, "get/set/access" in the
   ODB manual.

 * Support for bulk operations in PostgreSQL 14 using the new pipeline mode.
   For details on bulk operations see Section 15.3, "Bulk Database Operations"
   in the ODB manual. Note that while this functionality requires libpq
   version 14 or later, it should be usable with PostgreSQL servers version
   7.4 or later. The development of this support was sponsored by Qube
   Research & Technologies Limited.

 * Support for calling PostgreSQL stored procedures and functions. For
   details and limitations refer to Section 19.7, "PostgreSQL Stored
   Procedures and Functions" in the ODB manual.

 * New serial_connection_factory in the SQLite runtime.

   This factory can be used when the database access is guaranteed to be
   serial. See Section 18.3, "SQLite Connection and Connection Factory"
   in the ODB manual for details.

 * Support for attaching additional SQLite databases to the main database
   connections (ATTACH DATABASE statement). See Section 18.4, "Attached
   SQLite  Databases" in the ODB manual for details.

 * Support for SQLite incremental BLOB/TEXT I/O (the sqlite3_blob_open()
   functionality). For details, refer to Section 18.1.3, "Incremental
   BLOB/TEXT I/O" in the ODB manual.
